Definition: properly, fatness, i.e. by implication (literally) the loin (as the seat of the leaf fat) or (generally) the viscera; also (figuratively) silliness or (in a good sense) trust
BiblicalUsage: Kecel means the loins, the flank, and so by figure both folly and trust: Leviticus 3:4 takes the fat that is by the flanks for the offering. Job 8:14 says the hypocrite's trust shall be a spider's web. Psalms 78:7 says they might set their hope in God, and not forget his works. Ecclesiastes 7:25 says Solomon applied his heart to know the wickedness of folly, even of foolishness and madness.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe one word can hold both folly and trust because both live in the same place: the gut where a man leans. I hold that the difference is what you lean on: a spider's web, or God.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
